questions.worked_solution:
The Lotka-Volterra predator-prey model is given by

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=ax-bxy \\ {y}^{′}=-cy+dxy\end{aligned}
$$

where $a,b,c,d$ are positive real constants. Here, $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators.

With that in mind, let's examine the statements:

- The trajectory $\text{circles around}$ $\text{the nonzero equilibrium}.$

- From $A$ to $B,$ the number of prey $\text{decreases}$ and the number of predators $\text{increases}.$

questions.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=-2x+3xy \\ {y}^{′}=7y-5xy\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the Lotka-Volterra model above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the predators and $y=y(t)$ represents the prey. Find the nonzero equilibrium of the model.

$(${{field-1}}
$,$
{{field-2}}$)$
questions.worked_solution:
The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2x+3xy=0 \\ 7y-5xy=0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+3xy & =0 \\ x(-2+3y) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x=0$ or $y=\frac{2}{3}.$ We consider both cases separately.

- If $x=0,$ substituting it into the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}7y-5(0)y=0\,⇒\,y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, one equilibrium is $(0,0).$

- If $y=\frac{2}{3},$ substituting it into the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}7y-5xy & =0 \\ y(7-5x) & =0 \\ \frac{2}{3}(7-5x) & =0 \\ 7-5x & =0 \\ x & =\frac{7}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, another equilibrium is $(\frac{7}{5},\frac{2}{3}).$

Therefore, the nonzero equilibrium of the model is
$(\frac{7}{5},\frac{2}{3}).$

questions.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=-0.5x+0.5xy \\ {y}^{′}=y-5xy\end{aligned} $$ Consider the Lotka-Volterra model above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the predators and $y=y(t)$ represents the prey. Select the correct options in the reasoning below. $\,$ Evaluating the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0.2,\,1]^{T},$ we get
$J({x}^{∗})=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $\,.$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
$\,$ The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are {{field-5}}. $\,$ Therefore, the equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}$ is {{field-6}}{{field-7}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=-0.5x+0.5xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=y-5xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-0.5x+0.5xy)=-0.5+0.5y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-0.5x+0.5xy)=0.5x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-5xy)=-5y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-5xy)=1-5x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}-0.5+0.5y & 0.5x \\ -5y & 1-5x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0.2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}-0.5+0.5(1) & 0.5(0.2) \\ -5(1) & 1-5(0.2)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0.1 \\ -5 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix, we write down the characteristic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 0.1 \\ -5 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-\lambda )(-\lambda )-(-5)\cdot 0.1 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+0.5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation, we get the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1,2}=\pm 0.5\sqrt{2}\,\text{i}.$ Since the eigenvalues are purely imaginary, our equilibrium is $\text{a stable}$ $\text{center}.$

**Note:**
For the Lotka-Volterra model (as in this problem), it is safe to classify the nonzero equilibrium as a center when the linearization has purely imaginary eigenvalues. 

**Watch out!** 
In contrast, for a general nonlinear system, the Jacobian test alone is inconclusive (additional analysis is required to determine whether the equilibrium is a true center or a spiral sink/source).
